title: BotMachinePool
description: bot.machine-pool@1 (the pooled machines design, 2026-11-06): several of one owner's machines on the same local network that serve one model together through llama.cpp RPC, `rpc-server` on the members and `llama-server --rpc` on the head. OpenVibe.Network holds the record: the owner proposes it on /machines (POST /api/v1/machine-pools, two to eight of their own machines and an optional head; the default head has the most free VRAM), and each machine reads it with its own node token (GET /api/v1/node/self/pools/:id, network.node.self.manage) and approves it locally (POST /api/v1/node/self/pools/:id/approve with { certificate }). A machine's `certificate` is null until it approves on that machine: the Node generates an Ed25519 key there, keeps the private key, and uploads only its self-signed public certificate, which the other members pin for the pool's private link. A pool with any null certificate never serves. The record never carries a private key or a prompt. What a schema cannot say, Network and Node check at run time: the members are distinct and the head is one of them; every member has the pool's owner, today, through Bot; every member was seen from the same public address with a private address in the same subnet; the head's direct link probe to each member passes; each machine's certificate is its own; and any change of membership, owner, head or key revokes the pool, so all machines approve a new one. A machine that leaves (removed, signed out, a different owner) drops its link and its key at once.

id.description: The pool's id (ULID, Crockford base32). A pool is never edited: a change is a new pool with a new id.

owner.description: The person every machine in the pool belongs to. Pools of different owners are not allowed.

head.description: The machine that runs `llama-server --rpc`, sees the prompt and answers; it must be one of `machines`. The others receive tensors only.

machines.description: The members, head included, two to eight.

id.description: The machine (Bot's device id), resolved by Network from the machine's own node token, never taken from the body.

owner.description: The machine's owner when it announced itself; it must equal the pool's owner.

address.description: The machine's private IPv4 address and prefix on the local network (RFC 1918 only, a /8 to a /30), such as 192.168.1.2/24, configured on one of its own interfaces. The private link listens only here; never 0.0.0.0, loopback or a public address.

public_ip.description: The public address Network saw the announcement come from (never the body's claim). Every member must share it with the head.

port.description: The TCP port of the machine's private link on `address`.

free_vram.description: Free GPU memory when it announced itself, in MB. The head's default and each member's share of the pool's credits follow it.

free_ram.description: Free system memory when it announced itself, in MB.

hardware.description: A short hardware name the fit table matches measured speeds on, such as x86_64 or the GPU model.

certificate.description: The machine's self-signed Ed25519 public certificate (PEM) for this pool's private link, or null until the machine approves the pool on itself. Never a private key.
